plan.topic: Burping a lot on tirzepatide: how often the label reports belching vs placebo, and gentle habits that may help
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Burping more since starting tirzepatide? It's on the label.' By 6 s: 'Zepbound label: belching (eructation) in X%, Y%, Z% on 5, 10, 15 mg vs W% on placebo' (copied exactly), with the label's pooled population on the card: adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition, in trials with and without type 2 diabetes. Separate label fact: tirzepatide delays gastric emptying (no 'so'). 'Sulfur burps' is a commonly described symptom (no cause given). Untagged gentle tips: smaller meals, eat slowly, stop at comfortably full, go easier on fizzy drinks. Red flags, then the fixed don't-stop line, then the 11-16 closing with the Exp F line.
plan.why: A felt GI moment that has never had its own Short (the 11-10 long-form covered it only as a chapter). It stays within the playbook's practical-moment rule for 13:00 and feeds the Side Effects hub. | fact-check: Common, relatable side effect that's on the label, and a safe topic with red flags included. One population error: the Zepbound adverse-reaction table pools Study 1 (which excluded type 2 diabetes) and Study 2 (which enrolled only adults with T2D), and possibly more trials, so 'adults with obesity, or overweight plus at least one weight-related condition' on its own is incomplete. Copy the table's exact rates and the label's own description of the pooled population, and say it includes people with and without type 2 diabetes. Don't call it 'per dose' unless the table breaks it out that way. The gastric-emptying line must stay a separate label fact, never the explanation for burping. 'Sulfur burps' gets no cause and no source tag. NHS reflux/indigestion tips go only as NHS prints them, with their live reviewed date. Fizzy drinks: tag it to NHS only if the NHS page actually says it, otherwise keep it as an untagged tip. Emergency lines as written are good. Keep 'right away' and 'with or without vomiting'.

package.title: Tirzepatide Burping: What the Label Actually Says #shorts
package.description:
In pooled trials, 4–5% of people on tirzepatide reported belching vs 1% on placebo (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with and without type 2 diabetes). Smaller, slower meals, less fizz and stopping comfortably full may help.

Severe, lasting stomach pain, with or without vomiting, needs medical help right away. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

Source: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) US Prescribing Information, Section 6.1, Table 1 (Revised 8/2026): https://uspl.lilly.com/zepbound/zepbound.html
Full breakdown on our channel: https://www.youtube.com/@InforMedLab

#Tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe. I checked the key claim against the live Zepbound US Prescribing Information (HTML version, revised 8/2026). Table 1 in Section 6.1 lists eructation (belching) at 1% on placebo and 4%, 5% and 5% on tirzepatide 5, 10 and 15 mg. That table pools Study 1 and Study 2: 2,519 adults with obesity or overweight, treated for up to 72 weeks. Study 1 excluded type 2 diabetes and Study 2 enrolled only people with it, so "with and without type 2 diabetes" is the right population. The PDF version of the label also loads. The pain red flag matches the label's wording on pancreatitis ("persistent or severe abdominal pain"), and the fixed safety lines are copied word for word. The closing lines are in the right order and the Exp F and closing cards are correct for content dated 2026-11-16. The spoken word count is about 119, inside the tight 90–120 arm. The three minor issues below are wording or metadata polish, with exact fixes.

issues.claim: Zepbound US label, pooled 72-week placebo-controlled trials (Study 1 and Study 2)
issues.problem: The label says patients were treated 'for up to 72 weeks', not in '72-week' trials. This is a small difference in scope.
issues.fix: Zepbound US label, pooled placebo-controlled trials, up to 72 weeks of treatment (Study 1 and Study 2): adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, with and without type 2 diabetes

issues.claim: ...Section 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience (Table 1, eructation; pooled Study 1 and Study 2) and Section 5 (acute pancreatitis)
issues.problem: No scene is tagged to Section 5. The s5 safety line is correctly left untagged, so the title lists a section the script doesn't actually cite it for.
issues.fix: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, US Prescribing Information: Section 6.1 Clinical Trials Experience (Table 1, eructation; pooled Study 1 and Study 2)

issues.claim: Embarrassing tirzepatide burps are on the label.
issues.problem: The label doesn't call belching 'embarrassing'. The word is an editorial feeling beat, which is acceptable in a hook, but it leans toward shame, which doesn't fit the compassionate brand voice. This is optional polish, not an accuracy error.
issues.fix: Optional: "Feeling awkward about tirzepatide burps? They're on the label." (on-screen text unchanged: "Tirzepatide burps are on the label")
